Check of the calculation: Y = 1/(r + jωL) = (r − jωL)/(r² + (ωL)²). The real part is 1/Rp = r/(r² + (ωL)²), which becomes r/(ωL)² when r is much smaller than ωL, so Rp ≈ (ωL)²/r. The imaginary part gives 1/(ωLp) ≈ 1/(ωL), so Lp ≈ L. This is consistent with Figure 2 keeping the inductance labelled L.

Wrong choices checked by dimensions: (1) has no unit, (2) is in siemens and is actually the formula for 1/Rp, (5) is in Ω³, and (4) is in Ω but has r and ωL swapped. Each reason given in the explanation is correct.

explanationIssues: The overall explanation of choice (1) only says the field is not something that cancels (「打ち消し合う」のではなく) and that a single magnetic flux appears in the core (「単一の磁束として現れ」). It never states the correct version of the statement, so the wrong part of the choice is not clear. It should say this: clamping both the outgoing and return conductors together makes their magnetic fields cancel, so the load current cannot be measured. That is why you clamp only one conductor, so the fields do not cancel (「打ち消し合わないように」). verifiedEvidence: The question stem and choices (1) to (5) match the official figure word for word, including 「電線1本のみ」, 「数μVから100V程度」, 「抵抗を精密に測定できる」, and the swapped descriptions of the two resistance meters in choices (4) and (5). The only exception is the punctuation noted above.
The official answer table (令和6年度上期 理論) gives 問14 = 3, which matches officialAnswer.

(1) is wrong: you clamp only one conductor precisely so that the fields do not cancel. Clamping both conductors is the principle behind leakage-current clamp meters. choiceExplanations states this correctly.

(2) is wrong: putting an amplifier in front of the meter makes the input impedance (internal resistance) high, so the statement that it is low (「内部抵抗が小さく」) is the error. The explanation's point is correct.
(3) is correct: a Wheatstone bridge finds an unknown resistance precisely from the balance condition, when the galvanometer reads zero.
(4) and (5) are wrong: they swap what an earth-resistance tester and an insulation-resistance tester each measure. Both explanations are correct.
